updatingWhy: Kept a consistent accelerated-computing thesis since ~2012 and expanded it (reasoning compute, AI factories) as evidence arrived; publicly admitted error on quantum timelines; shifted China rhetoric with commercial interest.
rightReasons: Mostly right for the right reasons — understood that general-purpose parallel compute plus software ecosystems would be the bottleneck — though many statements are also sales positioning.

updatingWhy: Early, well-reasoned bet on OpenAI (2019); later re-negotiated exclusivity and moved AGI determination to an expert panel as the relationship and risks changed; skeptical of self-declared AGI.
rightReasons: Strong causal grasp of distribution, cloud and Jevons dynamics; weaker on near-term consumer search disruption.

updatingWhy: Moved from cautious slow release to rapid shipping after ChatGPT — a reactive rather than anticipatory update, but executed; candid that progress was getting harder in 2025.
rightReasons: 'AI-first' (2016) was early and correct; Google's caution in 2021–22 shows the gap between belief and action.

updatingWhy: Two large pivots (metaverse→AI 2023; open→selective release 2025). Both responded to evidence, but the metaverse thesis absorbed tens of billions before the turn.
rightReasons: Right that energy and compute scale matter; wrong that Llama would lead the frontier in 2025; open-source framing proved partly strategic.

updatingWhy: Small, consistent public corpus; shifted from quant trading to AGI research and stayed on an efficiency-first, open-weights course that events validated.
rightReasons: Right for the right reasons on architecture-driven cost reduction and temporary closed moats; corpus is too thin for confident scoring.

updatingWhy: Updated on open weights ('wrong side of history', gpt-oss) and on licensing; also re-framed earlier positions (non-profit → capped-profit → PBC) in ways that track commercial needs.
rightReasons: Very good on cost curves and scaling economics; aggressive on agent and AGI timelines; strategic incentives make some claims hard to separate from fundraising.

updatingWhy: Consistent scaling-plus-safety model since 2016–2020; dated, falsifiable forecasts (2026–27 'powerful AI', 90% code) that he has not walked back — updating is visible mostly in strategy (competing at the frontier).
rightReasons: Scaling-law mechanism correct; timing on code automation and labor too aggressive industry-wide.

updatingWhy: Stable long-term view (solve intelligence, AGI 5–10 years, 'one or two breakthroughs needed'); adapted organization (Google DeepMind merger) to LLM era.
rightReasons: Among the clearest causal models: search+learning, science applications, and caution that scaling alone may not suffice.

updatingWhy: Repeatedly re-dates the same predictions (self-driving, AGI, Optimus) without acknowledging misses; moved from pause-letter signatory to frontier racer within months.
rightReasons: Correct that compute scale matters and that AI risk deserves attention; timelines have been systematically wrong.

updatingWhy: Updated from independent startup to hyperscaler; reversed from building emotionally engaging companions to warning against 'seemingly conscious AI'.
rightReasons: Insightful on proliferation/containment; specific capability dates (hallucinations solved by 2025, ACI) were wrong.

updatingWhy: Dramatic, explicit, evidence-driven revision in 2023 (timelines and risk) after seeing GPT-4-era capability; acknowledged the radiology call was too early.
rightReasons: Foundational causal understanding of deep learning; labor and radiology predictions overreached.

updatingWhy: Highly consistent — arguably to a fault: maintains LLM skepticism and x-risk dismissal despite LLM progress; few acknowledged revisions.
rightReasons: Right on self-supervision; strong claims that autoregressive LLMs are 'doomed' have not been borne out by 2026, though unresolved long-term.

updatingWhy: The clearest documented belief revision in the set: moved from distant timelines to near-term risk in 2023 citing new evidence, and redirected his research (Scientist AI, LawZero).
rightReasons: Strong causal reasoning; many of his current claims are not yet testable.

updatingWhy: Champion of scaling who publicly declared its limits (peak data, 'age of research') when the evidence turned — an unusual self-revision; regretted the 2023 board vote.
rightReasons: Exceptionally early and right on scaling (2014–2020) for the right mechanistic reasons.

updatingWhy: Consistent critique; tends to re-frame progress as confirming his view rather than revising, though his 2024 predictions were specific and largely right.
rightReasons: Right about reliability and hallucinations and about price wars/commoditization; wrong about scaling 'hitting a wall' on capability.

updatingWhy: Updates in public and quickly: 'decade of agents' (Oct 2025) to 'threshold of coherence' for coding agents (Jan 2026), explaining what changed.
rightReasons: Excellent practical causal model of what LLMs are good at (Software 2.0/3.0, LLM OS); camera-only driving claim unresolved.

updatingWhy: Consistent human-centered and data-centric thesis, extended to spatial intelligence; skeptical of AGI as a term.
rightReasons: ImageNet bet was early and right for the right reason (data scale); world-model thesis unresolved.

updatingWhy: Remarkably consistent (Bitter Lesson 2019 → Era of Experience 2025); his 2025 claim that LLMs are a dead end sits awkwardly with LLMs being the biggest beneficiary of the Bitter Lesson.
rightReasons: The Bitter Lesson is among the most predictive ideas in the dataset.

updatingWhy: Consistent RL-centric program; adapted from games to math (AlphaProof) and to experiential learning for LLM-era agents.
rightReasons: Search + RL thesis validated by reasoning models; 'reward is enough' remains unresolved.

updatingWhy: Openly updated after o3 (Dec 2024), calling it a genuine breakthrough while keeping his core definition of intelligence; designed new benchmarks rather than moving goalposts silently.
rightReasons: Right that skill ≠ intelligence and that test-time adaptation was the missing piece; underestimated how far LLM-based systems with search would go.

updatingWhy: Consistent techno-optimist frame; positions shift with political alignment more than with evidence; job-loss skepticism restated without new data.
rightReasons: Good on commoditization and open-source competition; labor and safety claims are largely unfalsifiable so far.

updatingWhy: Has repeated the 'AI does 80% of jobs' thesis for over a decade, pushing the date forward; early OpenAI bet shows conviction that matched evidence.
rightReasons: Direction right on expertise becoming cheap; timing repeatedly early (doctors by 2025).

updatingWhy: Consistent skepticism of regulatory capture and hype; thin dated AI record.
rightReasons: Insufficient evidence to judge reasoning quality.

updatingWhy: Pivoted Inflection into Microsoft when independent economics failed; consistent 'superagency' augmentation thesis.
rightReasons: Augmentation view broadly consistent with 2026 labor data; Inflection bet on independent consumer AI failed.

updatingWhy: Explicitly framed uncertainty about market structure and updated views as it clarified; thin dated corpus.
rightReasons: Insufficient evidence to judge.

updatingWhy: Timelines compress with each statement (AGI 10 years → 2–3 years → 'much earlier') without reference to new evidence; sold Nvidia twice before major run-ups.
rightReasons: Conviction-driven capital allocator; claims rarely state a mechanism.

updatingWhy: Quantified forecasts are re-based rather than reconciled; exited and re-entered Nvidia.
rightReasons: Cost-decline thesis directionally right; valuation calls wrong in timing.

updatingWhy: A single, highly specific 2024 forecast framework; too recent to show updating, but its 2026 checkpoints (GW clusters, ~$500B/yr) tracked reality.
rightReasons: Mechanistic OOM-counting model; the early infrastructure checkpoints held, AGI-by-2027 is unresolved.

updatingWhy: Shifted emphasis from revenue gap to physical build-out as evidence accumulated, and stated the update explicitly.
rightReasons: Clear arithmetic causal model of capex vs revenue; the payback question is still open.

updatingWhy: Pivoted 01.AI away from pretraining when DeepSeek made it uneconomic — an evidence-driven but costly update; job-loss timelines unrevised.
rightReasons: Right that China could compete via efficiency; wrong that the 'age of discovery' was over in 2018.
